When a hybrid plant has its chromosome number doubled, this creates an allotetraploid (or similar polyploid) in which each chromosome has a homologous partner from the same parent species, allowing normal pairing during meiosis.  
This restores fertility because chromosomes can now form bivalents rather than unpaired univalents, so the plant can reproduce sexually.  
Option (D) correctly describes this outcome.

Final answer: (D)
